title: Program Structure
description:
## The Boilerplate
Every program you've written has the same skeleton. Let's understand it.

### `section .data`
This is where you store your data. Strings, numbers, constants. This section is loaded into memory when the program starts.

### `section .text`
This is where your instructions live. The CPU executes these top to bottom.

### `global _start`
This tells the linker where your program begins. Without it, the linker doesn't know where to start executing.

### `_start:`
This is a **label**. It marks a position in your code. `_start` is special - it's the entry point. The CPU begins executing here.


---
## Question:
What happens if you remove `global _start`?
b3t: The linker fails with an error
b4t: The assembler fails with an error
